closure_method.name: Section-Closure Method (adopted 2026-09-14, supersedes the earlier hard 0-unverified-candidate gate)
closure_method.rule: For every section: discover, reconcile against authoritative sources, resolve all P0 (blocking) and cheap P1 gaps, run the section completeness checklist, then close. A section may close with AT MOST 1 non-blocking P2 residual, deferred to DEFERRED_SEMANTIC_VALIDATION_QUEUE rather than chased to forced closure. Never defer an item that could change: (1) semantic control count, (2) mode/type universe, (3) control ownership, (4) conditional UI, (5) structural topology, (6) cross-system relationship, (7) resource workflow, or (8) another section's inventory -- those are always P0.

tiers.P0: MUST_RESOLVE_NOW -- missing major control, missing mode/type, semantic-universe-changing control, conflicting ownership, topology-affecting structural op, conditionally-exposed parameter, suspected-duplicate/ownership conflict, cross-section-affecting control
tiers.P1: RESOLVE_IF_CHEAP -- answerable from already-available evidence (existing transcript/screenshot/official PDF) without new investigation
tiers.P2: DEFER -- narrow, non-blocking, would require disproportionate effort; max 1 per section, logged to the deferred queue with full context

records.notes: OFFICIAL CORROBORATION ADDED (2026-09-14): the Xfer 'What's New in Serum 2' PDF's page 14 'Enhanced Macros' and page 15 'Enhanced Modulation Matrix' sections each list specific named sub-features (e.g. 'Source Curves', 'Aux Source Curves', 'Bypass Mods', 'Reorder Modulations') but never once use the phrase 'Macro Depth' or describe a third scaling mechanism beyond Amount and Aux Source. This is an official, page-numbered, feature-highlighting source (not just a tutorial) failing to name a feature it would very plausibly highlight if it existed as marketed -- meaningfully strengthens (though does not by itself prove, since this is a highlights doc, not the full manual) the merge decision below. CLOSURE M7 (2026-09-14): MERGE disposition -- resolved as NOT a distinct user-facing control; identity = MACRO.SYS.AUX_SOURCE. Reasoning: (1) the memory reference doc's own description of 'Macro Depth Column' -- 'macros control modulation amounts, not just parameter values' -- is behaviorally identical to the directly-observed Aux Source mechanism (a macro multiplicatively scaling another route's effective amount; MACRO.SYS.AUX_SOURCE). (2) The tutorial walks the Matrix row left-to-right in full (Source -> Source Curve -> Amount -> Bipolar/Unipolar -> Aux Source -> Aux Invert -> Aux Curve -> Aux Output -> Output Monitor -> Temp Bypass -> Delete) with no separate 'Macro Depth' field ever named or shown in that walkthrough, despite it being the exact part of the UI where such a field would appear if distinct. (3) No tutorial source independently corroborates a literally separate labeled 'Macro Depth' column. Given a full positive behavioral match plus a complete-row-walkthrough negative check, the best-supported reading is that 'MacroDepth' (code target mod_field_route_macro_depth) and 'Macro Depth Column' (memory doc paraphrase) both name the Aux-Source-when-source-is-Macro mechanism, not a fourth distinct field. Residual uncertainty acknowledged: this is an identity inference, not a direct sighting of a UI element labeled exactly 'Macro Depth' being absent -- if Step 6 MATRIX sweep's targeted UI validation later finds a genuinely separate labeled column, this record must be reopened (REJECT this merge) and split back out. Per CLAUDE.md 'do not treat code/state representation as semantic authority', the code target itself was deliberately NOT used to decide this -- the UI-observed behavioral description was.
